extracted.intended_audience: American colonists, delegates, and general public considering separation from Britain
extracted.subtask_description: A persuasive pamphlet arguing that the American colonies should declare independence now and explaining practical, political, military, and constitutional considerations for doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a constitution now while in our power
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is infinitely wiser and safer, to form a constitution of our own in a cool deliberate manner, while we have it in our power, than to trust such an interesting event to time and chance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a domestic constitution deliberately now to prevent opportunistic leaders ('some Massanello') from seizing power later; do not leave the seat of government vacant—delay opens a door to eternal tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity is the true source of strength
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is not in numbers, but in unity, that our great strength lies; yet our present numbers are sufficient to repel the force of all the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize continental unity over mere population counts—the whole united can accomplish independence while isolated colonies may fail; the present combination of numbers and unity makes action feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: The present time is the right time for independence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The inquiry ceases at once, for, the time hath found us. The general concurrence, the glorious union of all things prove the fact."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act now because existing military experience, material resources, and the present union make the moment uniquely favorable; delaying will erode advantages (experience will die out, trade and population changes will reduce unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and maintain a navy suited to American needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that America is especially well-situated and supplied for shipbuilding (tar, timber, iron, cordage) and that a navy is both commerce and protection: "Let us build; if we want them not, we can sell."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat shipbuilding as national industry and investment; a smaller, locally-focused navy (even a twentieth of Britain's) would suffice because American forces would be concentrated on home coasts. Consider using merchant premiums to keep ships ready in peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on Britain for future protection
rubrics_metrics.description: "Can we be so unwise as to mean, that she shall keep a navy in our harbours for that purpose? ... the power which hath endeavoured to subdue us, is of all others, the most improper to defend us."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-reliance in defense is necessary: Britain cannot be trusted to protect former subjects and could use 'friendship' as pretext for renewed domination; a distant navy offers little emergency protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation must be large and equal
rubrics_metrics.description: "A charter is to be understood as a bond of solemn obligation... I likewise mentioned the necessity of a large and equal representation; and there is no political matter which more deserves our attention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design representative institutions with ample and equal representation to prevent concentration of power in few electors or counties; small or unequal assemblies risk government by a minority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continental charter to protect rights of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A continental charter is "a bond of solemn obligation, which the whole enters into, to support the right of every separate part, whether of religion, personal freedom, or property."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame a charter (constitution) that explicitly secures religious liberty, personal freedom, and property rights for every constituent part as the foundation of long-term union and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government's duty: protect conscientious professors of religion
rubrics_metrics.description: "As to religion, I hold it to be the indispensable duty of all government, to protect all conscientious professors thereof... It is the will of the Almighty, that there should be diversity of religious opinions among us."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure government protects freedom of conscience and religious plurality; view denominational differences as harmless variations within one family rather than causes for persecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary expedients must not become permanent oppressions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Immediate necessity makes many things convenient, which if continued would grow into oppressions. Expedience and right are different things."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious that emergency measures adopted during crisis (e.g., methods of choosing delegates) are not perpetuated into abuses; plan institutional safeguards so temporary practices do not calcify into permanent power grabs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate the powers of representation and election
rubrics_metrics.description: Questioning whether "representation and election is not too great a power for one and the same body of men to possess?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When structuring Congress and modes of selection, consider checks that prevent a single body from holding too much authority over both representation and the electoral process; design for posterity, remembering virtue is not hereditary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable public debt if used to secure lasting government
rubrics_metrics.description: "Debts we have none; and whatever we may contract on this account will serve as a glorious memento of our virtue. ... The debt we may contract doth not deserve our regard if the work be but accomplished. No nation ought to be without a debt."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to incur national debt to establish an independent government and security for future generations; use public resources (e.g., sale of western lands) prudently to discharge such debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public lands to fund government and pay debts
rubrics_metrics.description: The sale/value of back lands and quit-rents could amount to sums sufficient to "sunk" the debt and "in time... wholly support the yearly expence of government."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply proceeds from public lands to pay wartime debts and provide sustainable revenue for government rather than taxing current population unduly; Congress should act as continental trustees for such resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence is pragmatically simpler and more practicable than reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: "That independance being a single simple line, contained within ourselves; and reconciliation, a matter exceedingly perplexed and complicated... gives the answer without a doubt."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor independence because it is a clear, internally-determined course, while reconciliation requires trusting a capricious external court and complex negotiations that may fail or be treacherous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay increases difficulty and risk of division
rubrics_metrics.description: "The longer it is delayed the harder it will be to accomplish... Should something not be done in time, it will be too late to do any thing, and we shall fall into a state, in which, neither Reconciliation nor Independance will be practicable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act promptly: postponement risks losing the current union, military experience, and political advantage, and opens opportunities for internal division and outside exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of false moderation that ignores sufferers' losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of conciliatory voices who "reckon without their Host" by imagining a return to pre-war conditions without addressing burned towns, private losses, and public debts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the real losses and sacrifices already incurred (towns burned, debts contract) when considering reconciliation; mere restoration of legal forms without reparations would leave the continent worse off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit commercial-defense synergies (merchant premiums to maintain ships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that premiums be given to merchants to build and employ ships mounted with guns so fifty or sixty such ships plus a few guardships could keep up a sufficient navy without heavy peacetime burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine commerce and defense by incentivizing merchant shipping to be convertible to naval use in wartime (premiums proportional to merchant loss of bulk), reducing peacetime costs while maintaining readiness.
